annotations.description: With 3 mana available (Forest, Ba Sing Se, Llanowar Elves), the player could cast Badgermole Cub (1G) which is a 2/2 that also earthbends a land into a creature with a +1/+1 counter, creating significantly more board presence. Instead they cast a second Llanowar Elves, which only adds a 1/1 body and mana acceleration. While ramping toward Mightform Harmonizer is reasonable, Badgermole Cub develops a much stronger board (2/2 + a 1/1 land creature) and the Cub's ability to generate extra mana from creature taps also provides acceleration. Additionally, playing into an opponent with Spell Snare mana open (UU available) is risky since Llanowar Elves costs 1 (not 2), but Badgermole Cub costs 2 and could be Spell Snared. However, they could also play Temple Garden first for an additional land, then have even more options. The sequencing of land drop before spell is also a consideration - they should play Temple Garden first regardless of which creature they cast.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Llanowar Elves (second copy) for G
annotations.betterLine: Play Temple Garden (paying 2 life or tapped), then cast Badgermole Cub for 1G, earthbending a land to create a stronger board presence. Alternatively, if wanting to play around Spell Snare on the 2-mana spell, casting Llanowar Elves is defensible but Temple Garden should still be played first.

annotations.description: The opponent has 3 untapped lands (Hallowed Fountain, Floodfarm Verge, Island) which is exactly enough mana to cast No More Lies (WU + 3 to pay is irrelevant - they can counter it). While No More Lies is already in the graveyard, the opponent could have other counterspells. More importantly, casting Mightform Harmonizer via Warp ({2}{G}) means it gets exiled at the next end step, making it a temporary threat. Meanwhile, the opponent likely has interaction ready with 3 open mana. Seam Rip (W) could have been cast first to exile a potential blocker or problematic permanent, and it's a permanent that sticks around. However, the bigger issue is that casting a Warp creature into open mana when the opponent is playing a UW control deck with counterspells is risky - if countered, you lose the card entirely (and with No More Lies-style effects, it gets exiled). The Warp version already exiles itself at end step, so the upside is just one combat step with landfall trigger doublings. Playing Seam Rip first (there are no valid targets with mana value 2 or less on opponent's board though - only lands) means Seam Rip actually has no valid targets here. So the real question is whether to cast Mightform Harmonizer via Warp into 3 open mana from a UW control opponent. Given the opponent already used No More Lies (it's in the graveyard), they might have Spell Snare (which hits MV 2, not MV 3 Warp cost). The risk is moderate but the line is reasonable to apply pressure. Actually, looking more carefully - the Warp cost is {2}{G} (MV 3), and the opponent has exactly the mana for counterspells like another No More Lies or similar. But the Harmonizer is being warped, meaning if it resolves, it provides a huge damage burst with landfall triggers doubling power. This is a tempo play that could be punished but also could be game-winning. This seems more questionable than a clear blunder.
